about: A demo run, replayed from a live gpt-6-luna run (1015-140835-6b21) at about 25x speed. The planner's question and every agent's edits and reports are that run's; in the live run the owner tried all ten model families, and here you choose. The tests, checks and budget caps run for real on a fresh copy of repo/. Code identical to the live run's gets the score already measured for it, from scores.json (LUCIDITY_RESCORE=1 recomputes them all, under a minute); any other code is scored for real. Agents were refused the held-out years; only Lucidity scored them. Data is from FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis): the target rate from the Federal Reserve Board, Treasury yields from the Treasury, unemployment and CPI from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
title: Fed rate hikes

card.ask: Will the Fed raise rates next month? From yields, inflation and unemployment.
card.why: Ordinary logistic regression on all 8 columns, no tuning. It's the best answer here without agents.

blurb: A model predicts whether the Fed raises its target rate next month, from Treasury yields, inflation and unemployment known at the end of this month, 1985-2026. The repo scores 0.462 log loss and plain regression on all 8 columns scores 0.342, so the goal is 0.3409. Ten kinds of model are tried at once, one agent each, tuning on 2005-2014. Lucidity scores every attempt on 2015-2026, years the agents never see, and recommends the best.
split: Trained on 1985-2004, tuned on 2005-2014, tested on 2015-2026. Agents never see the test years; only Lucidity scores them.

references.label: Coin flip (always 50%)
references.why: Say 50% for every row. Log loss charges 0.693 a row for that, so 0.693 means no skill at all.

references.label: Always guess the usual hike rate
references.why: Say the same chance of a hike every month: how often it happened in training.

references.label: Plain logistic regression, all 8 columns
references.why: Ordinary logistic regression on every column, no tuning. The five-minute model.

about_repo: bundled Fed-hike model: monthly 1985-2026, logistic regression, evals/score.py
commit_message: fedkit: hiked this month + 10-year yield, logistic regression, Fed months 1985-2026, evals/score.py
goal: Get held-out log loss to 0.3409 or lower (plain logistic regression on all 8 columns scores 0.3416; the repo scores 0.462) for predicting whether the Fed raises its target rate next month, without AUC dropping. Tune on the dev split. The no-lookahead tests must keep passing. Ask the owner which model families to try (plain linear regression with predictions clipped to 1-99%, plain logistic regression, naive Bayes, lasso logistic regression, ridge logistic regression, kNN, SVM, a single decision tree, random forest, boosted trees), then build each one in parallel and keep the best. Give each agent up to 4 rounds.

plan.summary: Tune and compare the requested model families on the dev split, then retain the best model that meets held-out log loss ≤ 0.3409 without an AUC regression, while preserving no-lookahead tests. Owner choices select which model-family experiments to run.

nodes.title: Compare owner-selected model families and retain the winner
nodes.prompt: Inspect fedkit's feature/model APIs and eval script. For the model families selected by the owner, implement each as an independent experiment in parallel, using dev split scores for tuning and keeping changes isolated until comparison; then integrate the best valid candidate into fedkit/model.py. Preserve the no-lookahead feature contract and avoid any use of held-out outcomes during tuning. Target held-out log loss ≤ 0.3409 with no AUC drop versus the repository baseline; run the held-out evaluation only as the final gate, alongside no-lookahead tests.
strategies: Plain linear regression (clip 1–99%). Implement ordinary linear regression as a probability estimator, clip predictions to [0.01, 0.99], and assess dev log loss and AUC.
Plain logistic regression. Tune plain logistic regression using dev-only feature choices and regularization settings; preserve probability calibration and compare dev log loss/AUC.
Naive Bayes. Implement a suitable Naive Bayes classifier with any necessary feature preprocessing; compare dev log loss and AUC.
Lasso logistic regression. Tune L1-regularized logistic regression and its preprocessing/strength on dev; compare log loss and AUC.
Ridge logistic regression. Tune L2-regularized logistic regression and its preprocessing/strength on dev; compare log loss and AUC.
kNN. Implement scaled k-nearest neighbors and tune neighbor count/weighting on dev; compare log loss and AUC.
SVM. Implement scaled SVM with probability output and tune kernel/regularization on dev; compare log loss and AUC.
Single decision tree. Tune a probability-producing decision tree's depth and leaf constraints on dev; compare log loss and AUC.
Random forest. Tune a random forest with conservative leaf sizes and class weighting options on dev; compare log loss and AUC.
Boosted trees. Implement an available boosted-tree classifier and tune its capacity/regularization on dev; compare log loss and AUC.

questions.question: Which model families should agents try? Select one or more; the recommended options are the strongest initial candidates based on the baseline information.

options.label: Plain linear regression (clip 1–99%)
options.note: A direct probability baseline; evaluate the clipped predictions consistently.
options.approach: Implement ordinary linear regression as a probability estimator, clip predictions to [0.01, 0.99], and assess dev log loss and AUC.

options.label: Plain logistic regression
options.note: A strong, simple baseline that already approaches the target.
options.approach: Tune plain logistic regression using dev-only feature choices and regularization settings; preserve probability calibration and compare dev log loss/AUC.

options.label: Naive Bayes
options.note: A distinct probabilistic baseline with low model complexity.
options.approach: Implement a suitable Naive Bayes classifier with any necessary feature preprocessing; compare dev log loss and AUC.

options.label: Lasso logistic regression
options.note: Can select among correlated features while retaining a linear decision boundary.
options.approach: Tune L1-regularized logistic regression and its preprocessing/strength on dev; compare log loss and AUC.

options.label: Ridge logistic regression
options.note: Regularization may stabilize the linear baseline with correlated inputs.
options.approach: Tune L2-regularized logistic regression and its preprocessing/strength on dev; compare log loss and AUC.

options.label: kNN
options.note: Worth testing, though the small chronological training set may limit it.
options.approach: Implement scaled k-nearest neighbors and tune neighbor count/weighting on dev; compare log loss and AUC.

options.label: SVM
options.note: A margin-based alternative that needs probability estimation and scaling.
options.approach: Implement scaled SVM with probability output and tune kernel/regularization on dev; compare log loss and AUC.

options.label: Single decision tree
options.note: Tests nonlinear splits with modest complexity.
options.approach: Tune a probability-producing decision tree's depth and leaf constraints on dev; compare log loss and AUC.

options.label: Random forest
options.note: Can capture nonlinear interactions but may be noisy on sparse hikes.
options.approach: Tune a random forest with conservative leaf sizes and class weighting options on dev; compare log loss and AUC.

options.label: Boosted trees
options.note: Flexible nonlinear model family to test against the linear baseline.
options.approach: Implement an available boosted-tree classifier and tune its capacity/regularization on dev; compare log loss and AUC.
